title: 1995 AHSME Problem 11
statement:
How many base \(10\) four-digit numbers, \(N=\underline{a\,b\,c\,d},\) satisfy all three of the following conditions?

(i) \(4{,}000\le N\lt6{,}000;\)

(ii) \(N\) is a multiple of \(5;\)

(iii) \(3\le b\lt c\le6.\)

solutions.text: The thousands digit \(a\) is \(4\) or \(5,\) and divisibility by \(5\) makes \(d\) either \(0\) or \(5.\) The pair \((b,c)\) is obtained by choosing two of \(3,\) \(4,\) \(5,\) \(6\) in increasing order, giving \(\binom42=6\) pairs. Thus the count is \(2\cdot2\cdot6=24,\) and the correct answer is C.
hints: Determine the possible digits \(a\) and \(d\) from conditions (i) and (ii)
Choose two distinct digits from \(3,\) \(4,\) \(5,\) \(6\) for \(b\lt c\)
